The Admiralty's consolidated decision architecture

THERE IS NO TEAM,
IT IS A YOLO!

Master decision tree · Eight connected diagrams · Decision references A01–H10

This master architecture consolidates the Admiralty's tournament decisions into eight connected diagrams. Each decision has a stable reference so that a setting can be traced from event purpose through configuration, scoring, administration, readiness, and final publication. Choices that make other branches unnecessary are identified explicitly.

FOUNDATION — must be establishedDEFAULT — normal arrangementOPTIONAL — opens a branchCONDITIONAL — depends on another choiceOPEN — needs definition

I. ADMIRALTY AUTHORITY AND EVENT TYPE

Diagram 1 establishes the controlling authority and the first branch: Pilot YOLO, the Road to the Grand YOLO, or a Special YOLO. It also defines how standing rules, season settings, event settings, round settings, and match settings relate to one another.

Decision register

ReferenceDecisionRule, dependency, or branch effect
A01Admiralty authorityThe Admiralty is the ultimate tournament authority before, during, and after the event.
A02Tournament typeChoose Pilot YOLO (standalone beginner event), Road to the Grand YOLO (multi-event season), or Special YOLO.
A03Season connectionFor a special event, decide whether it contributes to an active season. If not, there is no automatic season-standing or seeding effect.
A04Authority scopeStanding YOLO rules → season configuration → event configuration → round configuration → individual match settings.
A05Rule or exceptionA standing rule remains until changed. A one-time exception applies only to its authorized occasion and creates no automatic precedent.
A06Decision recordMaterial decisions should identify issuer, date, reason, scope, effective date, and the provision replaced. A unique order number is not required.
A07FinalityNo retroactive changes to completed matches or finalized results.
A08Administrative authorityThe Admiralty or its representatives authorize and administer events. Non-admin organizers are employees or assistants, not independent Admiralty authority.
A09Hosting privilegesAll Admiralty positions may host. Characters and their positions are used in narrative explanations, not as a rigid constitutional chart.
A10Conflict of interestAn organizer cannot adjudicate their own match. Conflicted matters go to the Admiralty or an appropriate representative.

II. THE ROAD TO THE GRAND YOLO: SEASON ARCHITECTURE

Diagram 2 connects the season calendar to regular-season standings, optional special events, postseason qualification, and the Grand YOLO championship. A twelve-stage season is one possible model, not a mandatory calendar.

Decision register

ReferenceDecisionRule, dependency, or branch effect
B01Season lengthChoose the number of stages/events. Twelve stages is an example configuration.
B02ScheduleChoose dates, frequency, and event calendar before the season begins.
B03Tournament eveningsChoose the number of evenings or sessions.
B04Evening structureDefaults: three rounds, approximately seven games per player, and a ten-minute starting timer. All are adjustable with notice.
B05Regular seasonDefine which events contribute to regular-season standings.
B06Special-event contributionFor each Race or other special event, decide whether its results affect standings and seeding. If excluded, its results remain separate.
B07Postseason decisionChoose postseason or direct qualification to Grand YOLO.
B08QualificationIf postseason is selected, determine entrants, thresholds, and any participation requirement. Top eight and six of twelve events are examples only.
B09Postseason structureChoose round robin, single elimination, double elimination, Swiss, ladder, King of the Hill, or another format. Determine series lengths.
B10Grand YOLOGrand YOLO is the season-ending championship and the Super Bowl of YOLO.
B11Championship formatRound robin is the preferred default; best-of-three, best-of-five, and other formats remain available.
B12Championship awardsSelect multiple individual award categories and define how season and event performance contributes.

III. PARTICIPANTS, DRAFTING, AND BATTLE CONFIGURATION

Diagram 3 shows how eligibility and registration lead to the confirmed roster, how battle teams are formed, and how the room is configured. The central distinction is that players form teams to play each battle, but the tournament is ordinarily calculated around individual performance.

Decision register

ReferenceDecisionRule, dependency, or branch effect
C01EligibilityChoose clan members, invited guests, mercenaries/stand-ins, the wider PC community, or a combination.
C02RegistrationChoose open registration, invitation-based entry, attendance-based entry, or another Admiralty-selected method.
C03Final rosterConfirm the participant roster generally about one hour before matches.
C04Draft methodRandom drafting is the default. The Admiralty may announce another arrangement, including fixed teams, for a particular event.
C05Draft frequencyChoose drafting every game, every evening, or another interval.
C06Team result influenceDefault: team wins/losses have little or no effect on individual advancement, seeding, or final standings. If included, define their exact influence.
C07Battle sizeChoose humans and bots by event/round. Examples include 2v6, 3v9, 6v6, and 9v9; no size is universal.
C08Vacant positionsBots fill empty positions by default unless the Admiralty decides otherwise.
C09Bot behaviorChoose intelligent moving bots, stationary bots, or another configuration. Decide whether stationary bots may fire.
C10Ships and tiersAll tiers are permitted by default; no permanent ship, consumable, module, equipment, or ordinary-play-style bans.
C11MapsSmall Tier II–IV maps are always approved. Other maps may be selected by the Admiralty.
C12Map selectionFixed weekly rotation is the default. Random or surprise selection is allowed when announced before the event.
C13Lineup visibilityVisible lineups are the default; hidden lineups may be selected.
C14Mode and timerTen minutes is the starting timer. Five-minute Armor Resilience is an available special format.
C15Room readiness/restartsSet readiness deadlines, host/room checks, restart grounds and allowances, and fault handling for the event. Beginner example: ten-minute no-ready period, two-minute restart-request cutoff, one ordinary restart per team; more complex series may differ.

IV. SCORING, FORMULAS, DOUBLOONS, AND PRIZES

Diagram 4 follows the scoring dependency chain from the question of what the event rewards through formula selection, required data, individual score calculation, prize-pool allocation, and final individual standings. Different rounds may use different formulas.

Decision register

ReferenceDecisionRule, dependency, or branch effect
D01Primary metricDamage is the default identity. Alternatives include potential damage, kills, torpedo hits, XP, credits, survival, objectives, Race time, or combinations.
D02Formula per roundDecide whether one formula applies throughout the event or whether different rounds use different formulas.
D03Formula sourceChoose the Excel workbook score calculator formula or another Admiralty-defined calculation.
D04Metric weightingDefine how multiple metrics are combined, normalized, weighted, rounded, and assigned precision.
D05Class weightingUse only when selected. Ship class must be known. DD=4, CA=3, BB=2 are documented examples, not confirmed universal settings.
D06Tier weightingUse only when selected. Define the tier value and exponent; its current intended role remains open.
D07Required dataSelect fields needed by the chosen formula. Common fields: result, player, map, mode, battle start, credits, Free XP, damage, XP, kills.
D08Individual scoreCalculate each participant's result from accepted values and the selected formula.
D09Doubloon calculationConvert or allocate individual scores into Doubloons where applicable.
D10Pool scopeA pool may apply to the entire season, an event, a round, or an individual award.
D11Prize commitmentConfirm real prize amounts and distribute the entire designated pool. The 0.54 conversion may be shown as public explanatory information, not a guaranteed cash redemption value.
D12Individual rankingTotal Doubloons is the intended ranking basis where the Doubloon system is used.
D13Tie-breakThe Admiralty determines ties.

V. ADVANCEMENT, SEEDING, BRACKETS, AND GRAND YOLO

Diagram 5 keeps individual scoring separate from the advancement decision while showing how standings become seeds, brackets, qualification, and championship results. Team victories and defeats have little or no effect by default.

Decision register

ReferenceDecisionRule, dependency, or branch effect
E01Accepted resultsUse verified individual results as the input to advancement and standings.
E02Advancement methodIndividual performance is the default basis.
E03Team resultsDefault: little or no influence. If included, specify the exact effect and any team aggregation method.
E04SeedingChoose registration order, random selection, performance standings, or a combined method.
E05TiesThe Admiralty determines tie-breaks.
E06Bracket formatChoose round robin, single elimination, double elimination, Swiss, ladder, King of the Hill, or another structure.
E07Bracket detailsDetermine byes, matchups, series lengths, consolation path, and advancement requirements.
E08PostseasonIf present, conduct the selected playoff. If absent, define direct Grand YOLO qualification.
E09Grand YOLO formatRound robin default; best-of-three, best-of-five, or another selected format.
E10Championship awardsSelect multiple individual award categories.
E11Bracket mathematicsFor single elimination: S=2^ceil(log2(N)); byes=S-N; matches=N-1; rounds=ceil(log2(N)). For 13 entrants: 16 slots, 3 byes, 12 matches, 4 rounds. A bye is not a match victory.

VI. OPTIONAL EVENTS: RACE, ARMOR RESILIENCE, AND SPECIAL YOLOS

Diagram 6 consolidates the optional event branches. If a special event is not selected, its dependent decisions are removed from that event's setup.

Decision register

ReferenceDecisionRule, dependency, or branch effect
F01Special event inclusionChoose whether the event includes a Race, Armor Resilience, or another special YOLO. If none, remove all special-event settings.
F02Race scopeChoose standalone Race or Race connected to a season; define any standings contribution.
F03Race scheduleEvery third week (weeks 3, 6, 9; week 12 optional) is an example, not a permanent schedule. Around one hour before matches and about thirty minutes are suggested defaults.
F04Race eligibilityLower 50% is a suggestion; the Admiralty may include everyone or choose another group.
F05Race map/routeOcean southwest-to-northeast is an example, not mandatory.
F06Race botsStationary bots are the general arrangement. Select their positions.
F07Race bot weaponsDecide whether stationary bots can fire.
F08Race timingUse inverse time, 1/t, as the intended measure.
F09Race modifiersFirst-finisher +10% and death -10% are optional, only when selected.
F10Race contributionRace damage counts wherever the scoring configuration allows. Decide its effect on standings and playoff seeding.
F11Armor ResilienceChoose before ordinary matches or as a standalone evening; set the five-minute timer, map, metrics, participants, and prizes.
F12Other special YOLOPotential damage, torpedo hits, objectives, or other Admiralty-selected metrics and formats.

VII. DWBOT, ADMINISTRATION, EVIDENCE, AND DISPUTES

Diagram 7 centralizes the shared operational workflow. It applies across event types so that evidence handling, communication, human verification, and final publication do not need to be reinvented for every optional branch.

Decision register

ReferenceDecisionRule, dependency, or branch effect
G01Event ownerThe event owner operates the system; local machine and SQLite are authoritative.
G02DWBOT accessDWBOT is owner-operated and requires the owner to have Discord administrator access.
G03Discord installationChoose standard channels and configure announcements, support, and communications during installation.
G04Participant browser readerPublish official versions, settings, scores, corrections, and other players' published results.
G05Evidence sourcesScreenshots are required; use replay files, OCR, and Python-generated reports as configured.
G06Required fieldsSelect event-specific fields from result, player, map, mode, battle start, credits, Free XP, damage, XP, and kills.
G07Participant checkParticipants are their own initial scorekeeper/referee/adjudicator and authenticate/correct values before submission. Submission is final when sent; there is no post-submission change window.
G08Human verificationThe Admiralty verifies results. The match/event remains provisional until all required values are verified.
G09Manual entryParticipant-entered manual values are permitted. No universal second-official approval or written reason/reference requirement applies.
G10RetentionKeep evidence for at least 48 hours; retain disputed evidence until the dispute is resolved.
G11Acceptance authorityThe Admiralty accepts, rejects, or corrects results. No reopening of finalized results.
G12AppealsThe Admiralty or a representative outside the competing teams reviews an appeal.
G13Conflict of interestAn organizer cannot adjudicate their own match.
G14Cheating/misconductReport privately and preserve evidence; exact procedure and sanctions remain to be defined.
G15Official releasePublish event settings, version, and effective date at least one hour before matches.
G16StreamingOptional; minimum two-minute delay. Five-minute delay and public VOD are not permanent requirements.
G17SpectatorsAllowed or excluded at the Admiralty's discretion.
G18Voice channelsPrivate team voice channels may be offered but are not mandatory.

VIII. DECISION PRUNING, READINESS, AND FINAL AUTHORIZATION

Diagram 8 shows how inactive branches are removed and all remaining requirements converge at a final go/no-go gate. Once authorized, the event proceeds through collection, verification, publication, and archiving.

Decision register

ReferenceDecisionRule, dependency, or branch effect
H01Selected configurationsConfirm all decisions required by the selected event type and active branches.
H02Remove inactive branchesNo season means no season standings/postseason/automatic Grand YOLO seeding; no Race means no Race settings; no bots means no AI settings; no team scoring means no aggregation; no streaming/spectators/Armor Resilience means their setup is removed.
H03PublishRelease event settings, rule/version reference, and effective date at least one hour before matches.
H04Confirm rosterConfirm final participant roster generally about one hour before matches.
H05ReadinessCheck prize commitments, room, host, map, bots, settings, DWBOT, participant reader, and participants.
H06AuthorizeThe Admiralty or its representative authorizes commencement. If not ready, correct the problem, obtain an authorized exception, or postpone.
H07Run and verifyCollect submissions, perform human verification, calculate individual standings and awards.
H08Publish resultsRelease final results through the participant browser reader.
H09ArchivePreserve event settings, outcomes, and evidence; minimum evidence retention is 48 hours, with disputed material retained through resolution.
H10Review next eventCarry forward standing rules, record prospective changes, and configure the next event or season.

Cross-branch dependency rules

A decision that is not selected should remove its dependent settings from that event's required configuration.

ChoiceWhat becomes unnecessary
Standalone eventSeason calendar, cumulative season standings, postseason qualification, automatic Grand YOLO seeding.
No postseasonPlayoff entrants, qualification thresholds, playoff seeding, playoff bracket.
No RaceRace map, route, bots, timing, eligibility, bonuses, penalties, scoring, and season contribution.
No botsBot count, AI behavior, positions, and firing decisions.
No team-result calculationTeam aggregation, collective scoring, team-based advancement, and bot contribution to a team score.
Single scoring metricWeighting and data requirements for metrics not selected.
No streaming or spectatorsStreamer selection, delay administration, VODs, spectator permissions.
No Armor ResilienceSpecial mode, five-minute timer, and its separate scoring setup.

Final operating sequence

  1. Choose Pilot YOLO, the Road to the Grand YOLO, or Special YOLO.
  2. Define season scope and whether special events contribute to standings.
  3. Set eligibility, registration, roster, drafting, battle size, bots, maps, ships, timers, and room settings.
  4. Select performance metrics, formulas, required data, Doubloon allocation, prizes, standings, seeding, and advancement.
  5. Configure only the optional branches actually selected, including Race, Armor Resilience, postseason, streaming, and spectators.
  6. Prepare DWBOT, Discord, the participant browser reader, evidence handling, human verification, support, and dispute procedures.
  7. Publish settings, version, and effective date at least one hour before matches; confirm the roster generally about one hour before matches.
  8. Complete room readiness and obtain Admiralty authorization.
  9. Collect submissions, verify required information, calculate results, publish final standings, and complete the event archive.
Governing principle: The Admiralty decides the purpose before choosing the configuration. The configuration determines which decisions are required. Unselected branches are removed. Completed matches and finalized results are not changed retroactively.
THE TEAMS FIGHT THE BATTLES.
THE INDIVIDUALS COMPETE IN THE TOURNAMENT.
THE ADMIRALTY DECIDES WHAT COUNTS.

THERE IS NO TEAM, IT IS A YOLO!

Working architecture. Version 1.0 · General reference only; the Admiralty selects the binding settings for each event and season.
